A.note: Strongest is that every metric is grounded in a declared annotation — statistic, supportPeriod, semanticRole, cadence — including the gap metric that catches silence no field can report; weakest is the one-hour tumbling window, which for an hourly cadence usually holds a single report and makes each window aggregate degenerate.

B.note: Strongest is the clean per-event/window split with a signed altimeter tendency normalised by real elapsed time; weakest is the hard-coded expectation of six routine reports per six-hour window, which converts a declared cadence into a completeness quota and fires spuriously at warm-up.

C.note: Strongest is the disciplined NULL handling, with every derived quantity guarded and never coerced to zero; weakest is wrapping the pressure rate in ABS(), which discards the fall/rise sign that is the whole operational point, and basing it on the omissible `slp` rather than the always-present altimeter.

D.note: Strongest is pairing the gust factor and spread with an explicit statement of why a maximum may be compared to a mean over the same ten-minute window; weakest is refusing any gap or missed-cycle detection, which leaves station silence entirely undetected while spending two outputs on the dewpoint spread and its closure rate.

blinding.why: A is the only transcript that quotes annotation keywords and specification prose verbatim — semanticRole values, supportPeriod with length and anchor, cadence kind and period, and lines about absent values being detectable as gaps and unlike statistics not being comparable — whereas C repeatedly states that no units and no cadence are declared at all.
